 Summary Bank of Baroda expects margins to improve towards the upper end of its 2.75-2.95% guidance by FY27-end, while stronger business activity in the second half is expected to support loan growth, says MD and CEO Debadatta Chand.
 Advertisement Remove Ad + Follow on Google Add as preferred source Bank of Baroda reported a 36% rise in net profit for the second quarter, driven by steady margins and strong loan growth. The bank's return on assets stood at 1.26%, marking some of the highest levels in two decades.
 In an interview with CNBC-TV18, Debadatta Chand, MD and CEO of Bank of Baroda, discussed the bank's financial performance, the impact of recent rate hikes on margins and the outlook for credit growth. He also addressed concerns regarding overseas operations and the bank's preparedness for expected credit loss provisioning.
 This is an edited transcript of the interview.
 Question Let me start with the margins. They are steady at 2.74%, a tad lower, but if you adjust for income tax refunds, is it higher than the April-June quarter of 2026 (Q1FY27)? Answer:
 It has been a consistent performance for us for the last many quarters, both in terms of topline and bottom line, although the June quarter net profit slightly decreased because of the settlement issue. Otherwise, the core has been quite strong since long.Coming to the margin, we said earlier it is 2.75% to 2.95% is the range that we look at, and last quarter if you look at the half year it is 2.76%. It is not because of any income tax refund, which is rather lower as compared to many of the quarters. It is the core income because the net interest income (NII) growth we are seeing at 9%. Obviously, when the NII growth is 9%, both for the quarter and also for the half year, it is a core margin which is helping the bank. Going forward, the repo increase was in effect from October 5. I think the October-December quarter of 2026 (Q3FY27) and the January-March quarter of 2027 (Q4FY27) margin is going to be much better. That is our normal estimate, but again will be in the band of 2.75% to 2.95%. Question Will it be at the upper end or lower end of that band? Answer:
 My expectation for the year-end will be somewhere at the upper end only. Question This quarter you get the advantage of one rate hike, and there are expectations of another in December. Assuming a 25-basis point hike, how much does a 125-basis point hike improve your margins? Answer:
 It could be significant. There are two factors that we have to account for. One is a quarter percent increase in the repo that happened, and 38% of the bank's book is repo-linked. Already that resetting has happened. Secondly, on a non-marginal cost of funds based lending rate (MCLR) book on the corporate side, a lot of resetting is happening both in terms of spread and also with regard to the benchmark yields going up. In that scenario, the margin income side is quite positive.On a rising interest scenario, the cost of deposits is slightly better placed because we had a significant foreign currency non-resident bank (FCNR-B) inflow. That has induced a significant liquidity which is parked as on today. That would allow me to slightly reset my deposit book with a lag. So that would be an upside for me. In that way, we are quite positive. Question Since your external benchmark linked rate (EBLR) book is lower at 38%, your advantage is a little less when rates rise. Is there any number in basis points we can go with for every 25-basis point rate hike? Answer:
 Assuming there is another rate hike maybe in December, the impact would be almost 10 basis points (bps). Question Was the FCNR-B inflow net margin accretive? In the end, it looks like everybody had to give a higher rate. Is it any better than a domestic three-year or five-year deposit? Answer:
 The FCNR-B rate can be between 650 to 675. Considering that most of the banks like us run a bulk portfolio also, and considering the current bulk rate and the earlier weighted average cost of the bulk deposit, this is margin accretive. It is obviously going to put less dependency on the bulk deposit, and that is margin accretive. But the impact would be felt in this quarter, not the last quarter. Question You will lend the loans in Q3. Should we look at very good loan growth for Q3 and the second half? Answer:
 Normally June and September are slightly slower quarters for us, but this time both have been very strong quarters. Both Q1 and Q2 have been very strong on the advance side and also on the deposit side. When I migrate into Q3 and Q4, these are typically business and productive quarters, and that is true for us for the last many years.Currently, the full-year gross domestic product (GDP) estimate is almost 7.6%. In that scenario, if you look at the retail demand in the market in terms of our own loan growth, and the published data on the unified payments interface (UPI) payment increase, we are quite positive. Although there are geopolitical headwinds, we are positive for a stronger growth in Q3 and Q4. Question Analysts will have a worry about the NMC Health issue. Is that over and done with, or should we expect anything unexpected because of the new case by BR Shetty? Answer:
 There are two values with regard to the overseas jurisdiction that is full and final. So, there is nothing more. Question So, there is nothing more on NMC Health, the company? Answer:
 With regard to the domestic case, this is as of today on untested pleadings. So, I won't comment on that. As far as the overseas is concerned, that is a full and final settlement. Question This is not the first time Bank of Baroda has had a problem with an overseas case. Will you wind down your overseas assets, or should we worry about more unexpected cases? Answer:
 If I compare as on today, let's say 26 vis-à-vis 21 on the overseas book, the overseas book was very less at that time. I think it was less than 10-11% at that time and today it is almost 16-17%. Contribution out of overseas operations was almost very muted or negative. Now the profitability is higher than the book itself in terms of percentage.Overseas operation always is a complex operation. We have significant tailwinds and at the same time, significant headwinds also to manage with that. As far as Bank of Baroda is concerned, we are very positive for our overseas business, and I have also given a statement that we need to expand now at this point of time the strength of the book. Question What is the contribution from fee income from insurance sales? Will you lose if the Insurance Regulatory and Development Authority of India (IRDAI) paper becomes law? Answer:
 That is a regulation concerning the insurance sector, not banking. Question Yes, but will it impact the bank? Answer:
 We have one entity which is engaged into insurance, and at the same time we do the distribution also. Obviously, whatever is proposed is going to impact the fee income, no doubt about it. But on a medium-term outlook, we expect there would be a huge increase in terms of the insurance subscriber base.That will compensate in terms of absolute amount for any drop in fee income out of the wealth business. At the same time, my percentage income out of wealth, particularly insurance, is very less as compared to the overall income. So, in that way, we are not impacted big time because of this particular issue. Question When will we know about the BR Shetty case? You said the global part is settled, but domestically, should we expect something in terms of provisioning? Answer:
 As of today, it is completely an untested pleading allegation. We also said in that particular press release that our recovery action against the individual would continue. We have also decreed in the overseas jurisdiction vis-a-vis the said borrower. In that way, it is very premature at this stage to talk about that because it is an untested allegation. Once a court process is set, then we will be in a better position. Question You have the money from the sale of National Stock Exchange (NSE) shares largely for expected credit loss (ECL) provisioning. What is the future impact on provisioning as you adjust to ECL, and can you guide on your return on assets (ROA)? Answer:
 As far as ECL, we have been preparing for long and we have been debating on the matter. As we speak on the book, the one-time impact is almost 125 bps, translating to roughly around ₹1,500 crore. We do have a floating provision of ₹2,500 crore that we made earlier.At the same time, the recurring impact on the credit cost is roughly around 30 to 35 bps on a gross basis, and on a net basis, it can be 20 to 25 bps. If you look at our credit cost guidance, we have given less than 0.6%. If you exclude the prudential provisioning we have done in this quarter, the credit cost is at 0.18.I think there is sufficient cushion for us to manage, but we are preparing ourselves. We have done precisely keeping all these aspects in mind, and because there was a one-off, we made the prudential provisioning. Question Your ROA is at 1.26%. How do you see it trending? What will the annual average be for 2026-27 (FY27), and is there any guidance for 2027-28 (FY28)? Answer:
 2028 would be slightly, but if you see Bank of Baroda's last 45 ROA, it is more than one, except the June quarter where the ROA went below one. As of quarter two, we are at 1.26%. For Q3 and Q4 again, we are saying that we are going to maintain a ROA of more than one. So, for three quarters, we will be maintaining more than one on a full-year basis.I said earlier we used to give a guidance of more than one, and that will be near to one for the current year guidance. On a long-term ROA projection for the bank, it is maintaining a ROA of more than one for the last many years, not quarters. In that way, we are quite positive of maintaining a ROA of more than one going forward. Question Your 16% deposit growth and 18% advances growth mean advances are running faster. Would you worry about the credit deposit ratio? What is it now, and do you have a ceiling in mind? Answer:
 In earlier years, we said the credit deposit ratio will be operating between 84 to 86. Considering we have a higher international book, obviously the credit deposit ratio is more than 100 at any point of time. But at the same time, the FCNR-B has really helped us in terms of moderating the credit deposit ratio, particularly for the domestic book.I used a word earlier saying that we have stored deposits, because you would have seen my liquidity coverage ratio (LCR) at 133%. In that scenario, even with the growth of 16% on deposits and 18% on advances, if you look at the absolute increase, the increase in deposits is more than that of advances. Considering you have excess, I think this is great to manage the liquidity profile or liquidity situation. We are very sure about the advance growth. As I said, we have better parked liquidity with us with the LCR at 133. Watch the full conversation here
